## Summary
Ring LLC is the Santa Monica, California maker of video doorbells and home-security cameras, founded as the crowdfunded startup Doorbot by Jamie Siminoff (Wikipedia dates the company to autumn 2013 [1]; Ring's own about page says it started in a garage in 2012 [3]) and owned by Amazon since 12 April 2018 [1]. Its 13 MA-L blocks [8] are registered to 1523 26th St, Santa Monica [2], and a MAC in one of them is a doorbell, a Stick Up / Floodlight / indoor camera, a Ring Alarm keypad, siren or sensor, or a Chime [1]. On the air these are always-on Wi-Fi clients: the entry-level and older doorbells are 2.4 GHz 802.11b/g/n only (Wired Doorbell 2K [4], original Video Doorbell [7]), while Floodlight Cam Pro and the Battery Doorbell 2K Plus are dual-band 2.4/5 GHz, the latter marketed as Wi-Fi 6 [5][6]. Silicon (SoC, Wi-Fi module vendor, image sensor) could not be confirmed from any reachable teardown or FCC exhibit in this session - iFixit's device page lists specs but no chip IDs [7] and the FCC databases refused automated fetches - so it is recorded as unknown rather than guessed, and no FCC grantee code is recorded for the same reason. Security history is about accounts and access rather than radio: the December 2019 credential-stuffing camera takeovers, the May 2023 $5.8 million FTC settlement over employee access to customer video, and the police partnerships through the Neighbors app [1].
